entities.title: A second Worker in this repository
entities.summary: The crawler is its own Worker, in crawler/, deployed beside the explorer's.
entities.context: The owner split the visualization into two components, the crawler and the explorer. The explorer's Worker has no dependencies by decision (worker no-dependencies); the crawler's AI step needs Anthropic's SDK.

options.title: A second Worker in this repository
options.consequences: Shares the database, bucket, tests and pipeline with the explorer; may have dependencies of its own.

options.title: A repository of its own
options.consequences: Versioned and deployed apart; the shared data layer would be copied or published.

entities.decision: A second Worker in this repository, chosen by the owner on 2026-11-19.

entities.title: Scans go through a queue, on Workers Paid
entities.summary: A cron trigger only queues work; every scan is a queue message.
entities.context: A big site needs more requests than one invocation should make, and a player approaching a stale address should not wait for the next cron run.

options.title: Workers Paid with Queues
options.consequences: $5 a month; a scan is one message, a long one continues as another, and rescans start within seconds.

options.title: The free plan only
options.consequences: Small batches every few minutes; rescans wait for the next batch.

entities.decision: Workers Paid with Queues, chosen by the owner on 2026-11-19.

entities.title: Repositories are reread by their history
entities.summary: A scan reads the head commit; only when it moved does it ask what changed and reread those views.
entities.context: The owner asked that repositories use git history to decide what to update. GitHub doesn't count a conditional request answered 304 against its rate limit.

options.title: Head, then compare
options.consequences: One request when nothing changed; the changed views only otherwise. A compare of 300 files or more counts as everything changed.

options.title: Reread every view
options.consequences: Simple, but a request per view per scan.

entities.title: Websites are reread by their caching headers
entities.summary: The crawler keeps each response's ETag, Last-Modified and lifetime, returns a fresh copy without a request and revalidates a stale one.
entities.context: The owner asked that the web use the standard cache directives. As a client, the crawler follows RFC 9111: s-maxage or max-age, then Expires, then a tenth of the time since Last-Modified capped at a day; no-cache and no-store make a response stale at once, and a no-store body is not kept.

options.title: Honour the directives
options.consequences: A site's own headers set how often it is read.

options.title: Fixed intervals
options.consequences: Ignores what the site says.

entities.decision: Honour the directives; the address's interval only says when to look again.

entities.title: robots.txt, a pause and a budget
entities.summary: Every request to a site obeys its robots.txt, waits a moment after the last request to the same host, and counts against a budget per run.
entities.context: A crawler that a site owner finds in their logs should behave as they would wish. A refusal such as 403 is final: nothing tries to look like a browser.

options.title: Polite by default
options.consequences: Big sites take several runs.

options.title: Fetch as fast as allowed
options.consequences: Faster, and the kind of crawler sites block.

entities.decision: Polite by default; a run out of requests queues the rest of the site.

entities.title: A fixed address for cooperating sites
entities.summary: /.well-known/cyberspace.json, read before anything else on a site.
entities.context: The owner asked for a fixed URL from which cooperating websites give their cyberspace data. RFC 8615 reserves /.well-known/ for such files.

options.title: /.well-known/cyberspace.json
options.consequences: A standard place; the file names a repository, serves a tree of views in the explorer's formats, or both.

options.title: A <link> in the front page
options.consequences: Needs the page parsed first, and a change to every page template.

entities.title: Addresses a site names wait for the admin
entities.summary: A cooperating site's own repository is crawled at once; other related addresses are added disabled.
entities.context: A well-known file is written by someone else, and could name any number of addresses.

options.title: Wait for the admin
options.consequences: The list only grows by what the admin allows.

options.title: Crawl whatever is named
options.consequences: A file could send the crawler anywhere.

entities.decision: Wait for the admin, except the site's own repository.

entities.title: A site can keep sections from the AI step
entities.summary: Paths a site lists under noAi are counted but their text is never sent to a model.
entities.context: Some sites will accept being mapped and not being read by a model.

options.title: noAi in the well-known file
options.consequences: The site decides.

options.title: No way to say it
options.consequences: robots.txt would be the only tool, and it also hides the section's existence.

entities.title: Each host gets only its own token
entities.summary: GITHUB_TOKEN goes only to github.com, GITLAB_TOKEN only to gitlab.com.
entities.context: A repository's host is taken from the address, which anyone allowed to add addresses chooses.

options.title: A token per host
options.consequences: No host sees another's token.

options.title: One token
options.consequences: Simpler, and leaks it to the other host.

entities.title: Claude Haiku 5.5 reads, at low effort
entities.summary: The AI step calls claude-haiku-5-5 with adaptive thinking at effort low, and a JSON schema for every answer.
entities.context: The owner chose Haiku 5.5 on 2026-11-19 over Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5: reading the 446 Festi sections once costs about $0.18 with it, against about $7 with Opus. It is weaker on mixed Icelandic text and judgement calls, which every reading's confidence records. Haiku has no server-side refusal fallback.

options.title: Claude Haiku 5.5
options.consequences: Cheapest; a declined or cut-off answer is recorded and that section skipped.

options.title: Claude Opus 5.5
options.consequences: The most careful reader, about forty times the price.

options.title: Claude Sonnet 5.5
options.consequences: Between the two.

entities.decision: Claude Haiku 5.5, set by AI_MODEL so it can change without a code change. A refusal, a cut-off answer or one that misses the schema skips that item; rate limits, server errors and lost connections send the message back to the queue.

entities.title: The model classifies; code writes the views
entities.summary: Claude answers small, schema-bound questions (a section's facets, a repository's parts); views.js builds the diagrams and records.
entities.context: Views must follow Meta/Agents/Skills exactly, or the explorer can't draw them. A model asked for whole diagrams can leave out a required field or invent a folder.

options.title: Classify, then build in code
options.consequences: Every view validates; a repository part whose folder doesn't exist is dropped.

options.title: Ask for whole views
options.consequences: More freedom, and views that may not validate.

entities.decision: Classify, then build in code. The classification scheme is the one tried on Festi; its facets are carried on each section's folder record for Cyberspace to shape buildings with.

sources.symbol: AI step: the views it writes follow the skills' schemas

entities.title: Direct calls, not the Batch API
entities.summary: Each changed section is one Messages request, made from the queue consumer.
entities.context: The Batch API halves the price but answers within hours, and its results would have to be collected by a later run. With Haiku a full read of a large site costs cents, and an approaching player wants fresh views soon.

options.title: Direct calls
options.consequences: Views within a minute of a scan; full price.

options.title: Batch API for scheduled scans
options.consequences: Half the price; views hours later; a poller to keep.

entities.decision: Direct calls, with prompt caching on the system prompt. Worth revisiting if the list grows to thousands of sites.
